title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 114
paragraphs: During this period, while Mardonius was selecting his army and Xerxes was in Thessaly, an oracle had come from Delphi to the Lacedaemonians, bidding them demand satisfaction from Xerxes for the murder of Leonidas and accept whatever he should give. The Spartans therefore sent a herald as quickly as possible, who, finding the whole army still in Thessaly, came before Xerxes and spoke these words: “O king of the Medes, the Lacedaemonians and the Heraclid sons of Sparta demand satisfaction of you for murder, because you killed their king, who was fighting in defense of Greece.” Xerxes laughed and was silent for some time; then, pointing to Mardonius, who happened to be standing beside him, he said: “Then Mardonius here shall give them satisfaction, such as is fitting for them to have.”
